And Prince Bohemond went out against them,

And in the year 584,
of the Arabs (584 A.H. / 1188 A.D.):
Saladin went in person against the fortress of the Kurds (Ḥiṣn al-Akrād / Krak des Chevaliers),
and waged battle against it for one day.
And when he saw that it was very strong,
he left it and went against Antarados (Tortosa).
And before all the siege engines were fully constructed,
the men of Aleppo gained control over its walls.
And the Franks held out in two towers,
and finally surrendered.
And Saladin destroyed the wall of Antarados,
and its fortress,
and its famous church of Mary, the Bearer of God,
and all its buildings.
And he went and encamped against Marqiyah,
and found it empty of people.
And he went against Jabala,
and the Arabs who were in it surrendered it to him.
And he went and encamped against Laodicea (Latakia),
and fought fiercely against it.
And the men of Aleppo made an underground tunnel beneath the ground of the city,
whose length was sixty cubits
and its width four cubits.
And when the Franks saw the tunnel, they were afraid,
and asked for terms of safety for their lives.
And Saladin permitted them to depart—they, their sons, their wives, and all their possessions,
except for livestock, grain, and weapons of war.
And Saladin took Laodicea,
and gave it to his brother's son, Taqi al-Din, the lord of Hama.
In those days, many Frankish warriors had come by ships from Sicily to the aid of the Christians.
And their commander desired to go out and speak with Saladin,
and he granted him permission.
And he went out and said to him:
"Behold, you have gained dominion over all these places of the Franks which are on the seacoast,
and you have left them but very little.
And it is not right for you to uproot them completely,
lest a great people burst forth and come out against you from the sea,
and you have great trouble with them.
Therefore, the neighborhood of these weak ones near you is more advantageous for you,
because they are a wall between you and those remote ones."
Saladin, however, replied:
"We are commanded by our law
that with all our strength we make our faith victorious;
and the Lord does whatever He pleases."
And that Frank left and went to his own country.
